messages:
Alice Chen: Quick intake — RedTeamX arrives next Tue-Fri (May 14-17). Need decisions on RBAC, KMS access, and audit-log capture. Vendor must NOT get plaintext secrets. Thinking ephemeral service account + staging cluster. cc @Marco @Priya
Marco Ruiz: We can do ephemeral SA + time-limited rolebinding. Suggest spinning up a 'staging-pen' namespace and binding a Role with only list/get/exec where needed. Example k8s RoleBinding we can apply:
```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: pen-test-limited
  namespace: staging-pen
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods", "pods/exec", "services"]
  verbs: ["get", "list", "watch", "exec"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: redteam-binding
  namespace: staging-pen
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: Role
  name: pen-test-limited
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: redteam-sa
  namespace: staging-pen
```
Marco Ruiz: We'll issue a token that auto-expires via projected service account token with TTL.
Priya Singh: We cannot give vendor KMS decrypt access for production keys. Options: 1) Provide sanitized artifacts, 2) Use a mock KMS in staging (preferred), 3) Provide signed attestation outputs only. Which route do we want?
Dan O'Leary: SRE prefers mock KMS + recording proxy. We can create a staging KMS key (separate project) where keys are never used to decrypt prod data. Also enable audit logs + export to our evidence bucket (retention 90d).
Alice Chen: Decision proposal: use staging-pen cluster + mock KMS. Vendor allowed to test there only. No KMS decrypt for vendor. Create ephemeral SA, rotate tokens after retest, and rotate staging KMS key version afterwards. @sec-bot please open a ticket.
sec-bot: Ticket created: SEC-2026-PT-3417 — pen test intake (staging environment, ephemeral RBAC, mock KMS, audit capture). Assignees: Marco Ruiz, Priya Singh. ETA: 48h to provision. :white_check_mark:
Marco Ruiz: I'll open infra PR for namespace + SA + network policy. Quick question: Do we need strict egress deny to prevent exfil or just allowlist vendor IPs? I recommend both: egress deny by default + allow vendor IPs for management.
Priya Singh: Agree on deny-by-default. Also enable VPC flow logs + SIEM ingestion. Add a SIEM rule to alert on >100MB outbound in 5min. And redact sensitive headers in HTTP logs (tokenize Authorization header).
Alice Chen: Evidence package we will require from the vendor: full audit-log JSON export, container stdout/stderr, k8s events, k8s resource YAMLs for exploited objects, and PCAP/network captures if any. They must provide reproducible steps. After retest we rotate staging KMS key and revoke SA.
Dan O'Leary: I'll schedule the retest window for one week after initial tests complete. Proposed retest: May 24-25. I'll update the calendar and assign oncall.
Priya Singh: Vendor asked about SLA for fixes: target to close critical sev within 7 days after retest; high within 14 days. We'll confirm in scope doc.
Alice Chen: Thanks — Marco drop the PR link here when ready. Priya I'll add the decisions to the PT runbook and attach to the vendor scope doc. One more ask: no production data in staging. If we need sample data, generate synthetic only.
Marco Ruiz: noted. Infra PR will include NetworkPolicy (egress deny) + SA TTL + mock KMS instructions. ETA PR by EOD tomorrow.
Alice Chen: Perfect. I'll send vendor the staging access instructions once PR merged. :+1:
